strengths: Systematic and rigorous empirical characterization of the SFT plateau across multiple data scales (200k-2.8M samples), providing valuable practical insight
Substantial dataset contribution: 3M chart-code pairs from real-world arXiv tables with 24 chart types and 1,555 APIs, significantly more realistic and diverse than prior synthetic datasets
Strong empirical results achieving SOTA among open-source models (83.8% high-level on ChartMimic) and competitive performance with GPT-4o despite 7x smaller model size
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including extensive ablations, multi-benchmark assessment, detailed low-level metrics, and out-of-domain generalization tests
Sensible multi-granularity reward design combining rule-based textual rewards (fine-grained code correctness) and model-based visual rewards (overall chart structure)
Exceptional reproducibility effort with detailed implementation details, exact prompts, hyperparameters, and supplementary code
Thorough documentation of data generation pipeline and filtering strategy with clear separation of SFT and RL datasets
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: MSRL combines existing techniques (GRPO, rule-based+model-based rewards, curriculum learning) in a straightforward manner without significant conceptual advances

Dataset quality concerns: all code generated by LLMs (Gemini-2.5-Flash) introducing potential biases; visual filtering relies on GPT-4.1-mini with only 100 manual verification samples; no human evaluation of code correctness across full dataset; potential copyright implications not addressed

RL evaluation limitations: very small RL dataset (33k, 1.2% of SFT) makes it difficult to isolate method effectiveness from data selection effects; multi-stage filtering introduces selection bias; expensive visual reward computation (72B model) limits reproducibility

SFT plateau analysis lacks depth: plateau could reflect distribution mismatch (LLM-generated→real charts) rather than pure data limits; no error categorization of plateau-region mistakes; alternative explanations insufficiently explored

Incomplete experimental validation: SFT baseline trained for only 1 epoch with fixed learning rate; modest out-of-domain generalization (257 samples) with 5-15% improvements; benchmark sizes relatively small (600, 500 samples); comparisons use 'updated' ChartCoder results due to flawed original evaluation

Mechanistic understanding gaps: limited analysis of what RL specifically learns beyond fine-grained details; no cost-benefit analysis of expensive visual reward computation; brief failure case analysis despite Figures E-F showing non-trivial errors

Reproducibility barriers: significant computational requirements (60+34 GPU-hours on H800s); reliance on 72B visual evaluator and specific rendering infrastructure; out-of-domain generalization demonstrated on tiny datasets

Generalization and scope limitations: model trained exclusively on Matplotlib; task-specific contributions; methodological insights limited to chart-to-code domain; 6.5% remaining gap to GPT-4o suggests substantial headroom
